title: Checks for temporaries returned from function calls in a match scrutinee that have the clippy::has_significant_drop attribute.
summary: The clippy::has_significant_drop attribute can be added to types whose Drop impls have an important side-effect, such as unlocking a mutex, making it important for users to be able to accurately understand their lifetimes. When a temporary is returned in a function call in a match scrutinee, its lifetime lasts until the end of the match block, which may be surprising. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Searches for elements marked with #[clippy::has_significant_drop] that could be early dropped but are in fact dropped at the end of their scopes.
summary: In other words, enforces the “tightening” of their possible lifetimes. Elements marked with #[clippy::has_significant_drop] are generally synchronizing primitives that manage shared resources, as such, it is desired to release them as soon as possible to avoid unnecessary resource contention. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for names that are very similar and thus confusing.
summary: In particular, the lint checks for names with a single character change. It’s hard to distinguish between names that differ only by a single character. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for functions that are only used once.
summary: Does not lint tests. If a function is only used once (perhaps because it used to be used more widely), then the code could be simplified by moving that function’s code into its caller. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Warns when using push_str/insert_str with a single-character string literal where push/insert with a char would work fine.
summary: It’s less clear that we are pushing a single character. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for lifetimes with names which are one character long.
summary: A single character is likely not enough to express the purpose of a lifetime. Using a longer name can make code easier to understand. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for string methods that receive a single-character str as an argument, e.g., _.split("x").
summary: While this can make a perf difference on some systems, benchmarks have proven inconclusive. But at least using a char literal makes it clear that we are looking at a single character. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checking for imports with single component use path.
summary: Import with single component use path such as use cratename; is not necessary, and thus should be removed. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks whether a for loop has a single element.
summary: There is no reason to have a loop of a single element. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for matches with a single arm where an if let will usually suffice.
summary: Just readability – if let nests less than a match. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for matches with two arms where an if let else will usually suffice.
summary: Just readability – if let nests less than a match. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for functions with method calls to .map(_) on an arg of type Option as the outermost expression.
summary: Taking and returning an Option<T> may require additional Some(_) and unwrap if all you have is a T. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for Vec or array initializations that contain only one range.
summary: This is almost always incorrect, as it will result in a Vec that has only one element. Almost always, the programmer intended for it to include all elements in the range or for the end of the range to be the length instead. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Detects expressions where size_of::<T> or size_of_val::<T> is used as a count of elements of type T
summary: These functions expect a count of T and not a number of bytes Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for calls to size_of_val() where the argument is a reference to a reference.
summary: Calling size_of_val() with a reference to a reference as the argument yields the size of the reference-type, not the size of the value behind the reference. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.
